title: Demand and Supply
text: Demand is the quantity of a good buyers are willing to purchase at a given price; supply is the quantity producers are willing to sell. Equilibrium price occurs where the demand and supply curves intersect.

title: Opportunity Cost
text: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made — a core concept for understanding scarcity and decision-making in economics.

title: Price Elasticity of Demand
text: Price elasticity of demand measures how much quantity demanded changes in response to a price change. Demand is 'elastic' if a small price change causes a large change in quantity demanded, and 'inelastic' if it doesn't.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level over time, reducing the purchasing power of money. It's commonly measured using a Consumer Price Index (CPI).

title: Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
text: GDP is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period, commonly used as a broad measure of economic activity/size.

title: Market Structures
text: Common market structures range from perfect competition (many small firms, identical products) to monopoly (a single seller with no close substitutes), with monopolistic competition and oligopoly in between.
